title: Traction alopecia in Ghanaian women: frequent heat styling carried the clearest signal in a 197-woman survey
headline: In a cross-sectional survey of 197 Ghanaian women (mean age 23), 41% had hairline recession consistent with traction alopecia; more than two heat-styling sessions a month had an adjusted odds ratio of 5.65 (wide interval 1.35 to 23.6), while keeping one style over six weeks was not significant.
evidenceTier: Cross-sectional survey, abstract read; full text not opened
fit: Hair lane: Partial. Population is African women; hair type is not stated in the abstract, and survey data show association, not cause.
displaces: Nothing to add; could prompt dropping frequent heat sessions.

summaryPoints: Observation (abstract read): survey in May 2026; 197 women; hairline status rated with the Marginal Traction Alopecia Score; 80 of 197 (40.6%) had recession consistent with traction alopecia.

Observation: more than two heat-styling sessions per month, aOR 5.65 (95% CI 1.35 to 23.62, p=0.02); age aOR 1.08 per year; style kept more than 6 weeks aOR 1.81 (95% CI 0.59 to 5.60, not significant). Model discrimination was modest (AUROC 0.68).
Inference: the survey cannot show cause; the wide intervals mean the 5.65 is imprecise. Recall and selection bias are likely in a convenience survey.
Limits: abstract only; young sample; hair texture not reported in the abstract.
toneData: African women (Ghana); hair texture not stated in abstract
fitLine: A cheap behavioural signal worth checking against own habits (installation length, heat frequency), not a new product or a verdict on any style.
